task.description: Produce the design artefact (lib/letflow/design/req183-webhook-delivery-dispatch.md or similar) for REQ-183's scope: (1) deliver/3(subscription, event_type, payload) -- resolve the plaintext-secret-availability question explicitly (see context note above) before specifying HMAC computation; compute an HMAC-SHA256 signature of the JSON-encoded payload, send as a request header (name the EXACT header/format chosen, e.g. X-Letflow-Signature: sha256=<hex>, and state explicitly this is Letflow's own choice, not an R-Co port, since R-Co's src/webhook/ is unreachable from this session); POST to target_url; classify result as SUCCESS (any 2xx) or FAILED (anything else, including transport-level errors with no HTTP status); persist exactly one webhook_delivery_attempts row per attempt with WebhookDeliveryAttempt's exact fields. This requires a NEW migration/schema for webhook_delivery_attempts (not yet shipped) -- specify it, tenant-scoped per decision 0003 Decision B matching REQ-181's webhook_subscriptions pattern. (2) On FAILED: increment consecutive_failures (REQ-181's schema), retry with backoff up to a configured max_attempts (name the default). On exhausting max_attempts, land in REQ-176's DLQ core via enqueue/2 with entry_type "webhook" and reference_id = delivery_id (NOT instance_id). (3) When consecutive_failures reaches a named threshold (state the exact number as Letflow's own choice, not ported), transition subscription to PAUSED + set paused_at. Explicitly name automatic post-event-append triggering as OUT OF SCOPE and a deferred follow-up (not silently implemented, not silently forgotten) since it requires a generic post-commit hook mechanism this requirement should not unilaterally decide. Design only -- no fenced code blocks reproducing real .ex content (this project's mechanical no-exceptions rule, hit repeatedly in this pipeline including on the immediately preceding requirement's design one run ago -- be deliberate about avoiding it).
acceptance_criteria: deliver/3 against a target_url returning 200 persists one webhook_delivery_attempts row with status "SUCCESS", http_status_code 200, and does not increment the subscription's consecutive_failures

deliver/3 against a target_url returning 500, and separately against one that refuses the connection outright, both persist a row with status "FAILED" and last_error populated (http_status_code 500 for the first, null for the connection-refused case) -- two explicit tests

deliver/3's signature is independently verifiable: a test computes the expected HMAC-SHA256 signature from the same secret and payload and asserts it equals the value deliver/3 actually sent in the documented header
a subscription's consecutive_failures reaching the documented threshold flips its status to "PAUSED" and sets paused_at -- driven by repeated failed attempts and read back afterward
a delivery exhausting max_attempts lands exactly one entry in REQ-176's DLQ core with entry_type "webhook" and reference_id equal to the delivery's own delivery_id, read back from the DLQ table

the moduledoc names the HMAC header/format and the PAUSED-threshold number as Letflow's own choices, explicitly not ported from R-Co's src/webhook/ (unreachable from this drafting session), and names automatic post-event triggering as an explicitly deferred follow-up rather than silently implemented or silently omitted
no route or controller file is added or modified, confirmed by git diff --stat scoped to this requirement's commits
mix test and mix compile --warnings-as-errors both pass with real output quoted
